subject: Environmental systems and societies

objectives.name: Show that you understand environmental concepts, methods and terminology, including the different perspectives people bring to an issue.
Use your understanding to analyse explanations, evidence, models and case studies, including the arguments and values involved.
Evaluate explanations, proposed solutions and investigation methods; justify your judgments and connect the political, economic, ethical and social contexts.
Investigate a sustainability issue by defining a workable environmental research question and using suitable methods ethically.

components.name: Individual investigation (SL)

criteria.name: Research question and inquiry
criteria.guidance: Name the environmental issue and the question, and show why it is worth investigating.

criteria.name: Strategy and tension
criteria.guidance: New in the 2026 guide and the differentiator. Show how competing perspectives change the outcome of a strategy.

criteria.name: Method
criteria.guidance: Appropriate to the question and repeatable by someone else from what you wrote.

criteria.name: Treatment of data
criteria.guidance: Process and present the data so it can be read, uncertainties included.

criteria.name: Analysis and conclusion
criteria.guidance: Interpret what the data shows and answer your own question, only as far as it supports.

criteria.name: Evaluation
criteria.guidance: Limitations that actually mattered, improvements that address them, and what is still open.

notes: 3,000 words maximum, up from 2,250 under the previous guide. 30 marks across six criteria A-F, common at SL and HL. Ten hours.
Criterion NAMES are corroborated; the per-criterion split is NOT — one source gives 4/4/4/6/6/6, another states it is unpublished. No marks are claimed.
Criterion B (strategy and tension) is new in the 2026 guide and has no legacy exemplars. Treating this as a Biology IA with an environmental topic forfeits it entirely.
Group collaboration is permitted if variables differ and each student's data is their own.

Two independently hosted matching IB briefs confirm eight syllabus topics, the three named Foundation subtopics and three HL-only lenses. The earlier absence note’s reference to seven topics was incorrect. Practical work and inquiry skills are integrated activities, not additional syllabus topics.

AO1–AO4 are Albus’s own second-person paraphrases of the 2026 brief. AO4 concerns an ethical investigation of a sustainability issue; it is not evidence that each exam paper assesses all four objectives. The briefs give component percentages, not whole-subject per-AO weightings, so objective weights remain null.
